en.title: Land reform, democracy, and changing regional power
en.summary: The Bihar Land Reforms Act of 1950 marked a constitutional break in the agrarian order of north Bihar. It provided for the transfer to the state of the interests of proprietors and tenure-holders, dismantling the legal position of zamindars as revenue-receiving intermediaries.

mai.title: भूमि-सुधार, लोकतन्त्र आ बदलैत क्षेत्रीय शक्ति
mai.summary: ई अध्याय “भूमि-सुधार, लोकतन्त्र आ बदलैत क्षेत्रीय शक्ति” विषयक स्वातंत्र्योत्तर राजनीति, सीमांचल, भाषा, कला, नदी, पर्यावरण आ नागरिकताक स्रोत-आधारित ऐतिहासिक पड़ताल करैत अछि।

outline: The end of zamindari
Constitutional land reform and the early Republic
What vesting transferred
Darbhanga Raj and the Kameshwar Singh litigation

en.title: The India-Nepal borderland, migration, and exchange
en.summary: The India–Nepal frontier is often described as 'open', but openness is a historically specific regulatory arrangement rather than the absence of a boundary. The two states retain separate sovereignty, citizenship, criminal and civil jurisdiction, taxation, property law, electoral membership, customs systems, and security institutions. What is unusual is the extent to which citizens can move across much of the land frontier without the passport-and-visa regime typical of many international borders.

mai.title: भारत-नेपाल सीमांचल, प्रवासन आ आदान-प्रदान
mai.summary: ई अध्याय “भारत-नेपाल सीमांचल, प्रवासन आ आदान-प्रदान” विषयक स्वातंत्र्योत्तर राजनीति, सीमांचल, भाषा, कला, नदी, पर्यावरण आ नागरिकताक स्रोत-आधारित ऐतिहासिक पड़ताल करैत अछि।

outline: An open border is still a border
Article 7 and the limits of treaty shorthand
Open-border practice before and after 1950
Paired localities rather than one undifferentiated frontier

en.title: Maithili and Angika: language, literature, and recognition
en.summary: Language recognition in modern South Asia occurs through several institutions that answer different questions. A university may accept a language for examination; a literary academy may recognize it for awards and publication; a census may classify a returned mother tongue under a particular heading; a state may authorize official use for specified purposes; the Constitution may place a language in the Eighth Schedule; and a digital standard may encode a historical script.

mai.title: मैथिली आ अंगिका: भाषा, साहित्य आ मान्यता
mai.summary: ई अध्याय “मैथिली आ अंगिका: भाषा, साहित्य आ मान्यता” विषयक स्वातंत्र्योत्तर राजनीति, सीमांचल, भाषा, कला, नदी, पर्यावरण आ नागरिकताक स्रोत-आधारित ऐतिहासिक पड़ताल करैत अछि।

outline: Recognition is not one event
Names, varieties, and the danger of retrospective certainty
Grierson and the colonial linguistic survey
Chhika-Chhiki, Bhagalpuri speech, and the later Angika name

en.title: Mithila painting, gender, and the cultural economy
en.summary: Mithila painting is best understood as a history of linked media rather than as a single object with a single origin date. Wall murals, floor drawings, wedding-room images, paper paintings, textiles, books, public murals, museum acquisitions, and digital reproductions belong to different material and institutional settings. Their connections are real, but the historical record does not justify treating every modern paper painting as an unchanged survival from an ancient age.

mai.title: मिथिला चित्रकला, लैंगिकता आ सांस्कृतिक अर्थव्यवस्था
mai.summary: ई अध्याय “मिथिला चित्रकला, लैंगिकता आ सांस्कृतिक अर्थव्यवस्था” विषयक स्वातंत्र्योत्तर राजनीति, सीमांचल, भाषा, कला, नदी, पर्यावरण आ नागरिकताक स्रोत-आधारित ऐतिहासिक पड़ताल करैत अछि।

outline: From domestic surfaces to a modern art field
What the evidence can and cannot date
The 1919 marriage paintings: an early documentary anchor
The 1934 earthquake and an accidental archive

en.title: The Kosi, floods, infrastructure, and environmental risk
en.summary: The Kosi is not a backdrop to the history of Mithila. It has shaped settlement, agrarian opportunity, transport, administrative boundaries, public works, migration, and political expectations. Yet a river is not an intentional political actor. Historical explanation must connect geomorphology and monsoon hydrology with institutions that decide where people may live, which structures are maintained, how warnings move, and whose losses are compensated.

mai.title: कोसी, बाढ़ि, आधारभूत संरचना आ पर्यावरणीय जोखिम
mai.summary: ई अध्याय “कोसी, बाढ़ि, आधारभूत संरचना आ पर्यावरणीय जोखिम” विषयक स्वातंत्र्योत्तर राजनीति, सीमांचल, भाषा, कला, नदी, पर्यावरण आ नागरिकताक स्रोत-आधारित ऐतिहासिक पड़ताल करैत अछि।

outline: A river system as a historical actor
The Sapt Kosi basin: one river assembled from many headwaters
From mountain gradient to the Gangetic plain
The Kosi megafan and the language of avulsion

en.title: Madhesh, representation, and plural citizenship in Nepal
en.summary: Madhesh is indispensable to the modern political history of Nepal, but it must be handled as a historically changing category. The word has older geographical usages, yet the broad political macro-category 'Madheshi' acquired greatly increased institutional and electoral salience after the restoration of multiparty politics in 1990. David Gellner has accordingly emphasized that the post-1990 period produced new large-scale categories of political classification, even where the words themselves were not wholly new.

mai.title: मधेश, प्रतिनिधित्व आ नेपालमे बहुल नागरिकता
mai.summary: ई अध्याय “मधेश, प्रतिनिधित्व आ नेपालमे बहुल नागरिकता” विषयक स्वातंत्र्योत्तर राजनीति, सीमांचल, भाषा, कला, नदी, पर्यावरण आ नागरिकताक स्रोत-आधारित ऐतिहासिक पड़ताल करैत अछि।

outline: A modern political category, not an ancient homogeneous people
Madhesh, Tarai, and Mithila overlap without becoming synonyms
The borderland existed before modern citizenship documents
From Rana rule to statutory citizenship

en.title: Conclusions: connected histories without false unity
en.summary: Mithila, Vajji, and Anga do not form a single continuous state, ethnicity, language zone, or administrative unit. They belong to different historical scales and to different moments of political vocabulary. Their histories intersect through the middle and lower Ganga plain, Himalayan foothills, river systems, religious routes, courts, languages, manuscript cultures, landed institutions, markets, migration, and the modern India–Nepal border.

mai.title: निष्कर्ष: मिथ्या एकरूपता बिना जुड़ल इतिहास
mai.summary: ई अध्याय स्वातंत्र्योत्तर राजनीति, सीमांचल, भाषा, कला, नदी, पर्यावरण आ नागरिकताक मुख्य निष्कर्ष समेटि मिथ्या कालातीत एकरूपताक बदला ऐतिहासिक सम्बन्ध, परिवर्तन आ भिन्नता स्पष्ट करैत अछि।

outline: Three names, many scales
Connected history is not a claim of sameness
No single territorial line can contain the whole history
Region is a relationship before it is a polygon
